correctness.rationale: Read frozen RESULT.md and check.py. For a real-linear complex representation xi↦z xi+w conj(xi), determinant |z|²−|w|², singular values |z|±|w|, and Hilbert–Schmidt metric 2(|z|²+|w|²) are exact. A nonsingular real projective line forces a fixed determinant sign and hence a contraction graph over its positive coordinate plane. The monotone singular-value ratio G attains its supremum at norm L=rho. Tangents of the two principal angles are the singular values of L, giving the stated projector difference. Taylor expansion gives (q−p)/2 rho² for finite q, rho for q=∞. Independent 4-D projection test rho=0.6 gave gap 0.5144957554 and checked several p,q boundaries.

value.rationale: Replaces a previously known single Gelfand number with the entire Grassmannian objective and sharp optimizer stability. The finite-q versus operator-norm linear/quadratic transition is a structurally motivated endpoint phenomenon and useful for nearly extremal matrix subspaces.

final_claim: For every real 2-plane E in M_2(R), 0<p<q<=infinity, Phi(E)=1 if E meets the singular cone; otherwise E is a graph over one of two conformal planes with norm rho<1 and Phi(E)=G_{p,q}(rho). The projection gap is rho/sqrt(1+rho^2), uniquely optimizing planes are the two conformal planes, and local loss is quadratic at finite q and linear for q=infinity.
